SEARCH
Package com.falkordb

Interface GraphContext.Pipeline

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable, Closeable
Enclosing interface:
GraphContext
public static interface GraphContext.Pipeline extends Closeable
A pipeline on a GraphContext's connection: commands are sent as they are queued, and their replies are read together, by sync(), syncAndReturnAll() or close(). Each command returns a Reply, which can be read once its reply has been read off the connection. Get one with GraphContext.pipeline(): 

 try (GraphContext context = graph.getContext()) {
     GraphContext.Pipeline pipeline = context.pipeline();
     pipeline.sendCommand("SET", "visits", "1");
     Reply<ResultSet> created = pipeline.query("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Alice'})");
     Reply<Object> visits = pipeline.sendCommand("INCR", "visits");
     pipeline.sync();
     System.out.println(created.get().getStatistics().nodesCreated() + " node, " + visits.get() + " visits");
 }

A graph reply is decoded when it is read, as for the deprecated GraphPipeline, which describes how a deleteGraph() affects the replies queued before it. A reply that fails to decode throws the same exception on every Reply.get(). As in the rest of the client's API, the server's error replies are GraphExceptions, and a connection that can't be opened, or fails, throws a FalkorDBConnectionException.

While the pipeline awaits replies, the context's connection is its own: the context runs none of its own commands, and no other pipeline or transaction can be started or used on it, since what they sent would be read as this pipeline's replies. Each throws an IllegalStateException instead, as does queuing a command once the pipeline is closed, a read of it failed, or the context is closed.

Like its context, a pipeline is meant for one thread. Read what it queued before dropping it: closing the context reads the replies a pipeline still awaits, which then can be read.

    • query

      Reply<ResultSet> query(String query, long timeout)
      Queues a Cypher query with a timeout.

      The timeout is sent with the query and limits how long the server runs it; 0 sets none, so the server's default (TIMEOUT_DEFAULT) applies. It doesn't change how long the client waits for the replies in sync() or syncAndReturnAll(), which a socket (read) timeout on the connection can still end: see Graph.query(String, long).

      Parameters:
      query - Cypher query
      timeout - timeout in milliseconds; not negative
      Returns:
      the reply: the result set
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if timeout is negative; nothing is queued then

      Reply<Long> waitReplicas(int replicas, long timeout)
      Queues a WAIT, which blocks until the writes before it are acknowledged by at least replicas replicas, or the timeout has passed. The pipeline's read waits for it.

    • sendCommand

      Reply<@Nullable Object> sendCommand(String command, String... args)
      Queues a Redis command that isn't a graph command, such as SET, GET or INCR, to run with the graph commands.

      The reply is decoded from what the server sent into JDK types: a simple or bulk string as a UTF-8 String, an integer as a Long, an array as a List of its elements decoded the same way, with a GraphException where an element is an error, and a nil reply as null. The driver speaks RESP2 unless its connection URI asks for protocol=3; then a double is a Double, a boolean a Boolean, a big number a java.math.BigInteger, a set a List and a map a LinkedHashMap, except an empty map, which is an empty List. An error reply makes reading the reply throw a GraphException.

      A command that would break this pipeline, the connection or the client's schema cache is refused with an IllegalArgumentException, and nothing is sent. Command names are compared ignoring the case of ASCII letters, as Redis does:

      • commands this API runs itself: MULTI, EXEC, DISCARD, WATCH and UNWATCH (see GraphContext.transaction() and GraphContext.watch(String...)), WAIT (see waitReplicas(int, long)), and every GRAPH.* command, whose reply only the graph methods decode, with the client's schema cache, which they keep up to date;
      • commands that delete or replace the graph's key behind that cache, which would then decode a new graph's replies with the old graph's names: DEL, UNLINK, GETDEL, RENAME, RENAMENX, MOVE, RESTORE and MIGRATE of the graph's key, COPY to it, and FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB and SWAPDB; delete the graph with deleteGraph(). Other commands that write the graph's key aren't recognized: see below;
      • commands that change the connection's state, which outlives the context when the pool lends the connection on, or how its replies are framed: AUTH, HELLO, SELECT, CLIENT, RESET, QUIT, READONLY, READWRITE, ASKING, SCRIPT DEBUG;
      • commands that take the connection out of request and reply: SUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE, SSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PUNSUBSCRIBE, SUNSUBSCRIBE, MONITOR, SYNC, PSYNC, REPLCONF;
      • blocking commands, which hold the connection in a pipeline, so that closing the context waits for them, and don't block inside MULTI: BLPOP, BRPOP, BRPOPLPUSH, BLMOVE, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN, BZPOPMAX, BZMPOP, WAITAOF, DEBUG SLEEP, and XREAD or XREADGROUP with BLOCK.

      Some of these may be allowed in a later release, such as the GRAPH.* commands that don't touch a graph. Other commands are sent as they are: an overwrite of the graph's key, such as a SET of it, or its expiry, still leaves the schema cache as it was, as a change by another client would. In a cluster the context's connection is to the node that serves the graph's key, so a command on a key in another hash slot fails with a MOVED error; put the graph's name in the key as a hash tag to keep it on that node.

      Parameters:
      command - the command's name, such as "SET"
      args - its arguments
      Returns:
      the reply
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the command is refused, command is null or empty, or args or one of its elements is null; nothing is queued then

    • sendBinaryCommand

      Reply<@Nullable Object> sendBinaryCommand(String command, byte[]... args)
      Queues a Redis command that isn't a graph command, with binary arguments, such as a SET of a binary value.

      The reply is decoded from what the server sent into JDK types: a simple or bulk string as a byte[], an integer as a Long, an array as a List of its elements decoded the same way, with a GraphException where an element is an error, and a nil reply as null. The driver speaks RESP2 unless its connection URI asks for protocol=3; then a double is a Double, a boolean a Boolean, a big number a java.math.BigInteger, a set a List and a map a LinkedHashMap (whose byte[] keys compare by identity), except an empty map, which is an empty List. An error reply makes reading the reply throw a GraphException.

      A command that would break this pipeline, the connection or the client's schema cache is refused with an IllegalArgumentException, and nothing is sent. Command names are compared ignoring the case of ASCII letters, as Redis does:

      • commands this API runs itself: MULTI, EXEC, DISCARD, WATCH and UNWATCH (see GraphContext.transaction() and GraphContext.watch(String...)), WAIT (see waitReplicas(int, long)), and every GRAPH.* command, whose reply only the graph methods decode, with the client's schema cache, which they keep up to date;
      • commands that delete or replace the graph's key behind that cache, which would then decode a new graph's replies with the old graph's names: DEL, UNLINK, GETDEL, RENAME, RENAMENX, MOVE, RESTORE and MIGRATE of the graph's key, COPY to it, and FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB and SWAPDB; delete the graph with deleteGraph(). Other commands that write the graph's key aren't recognized: see below;
      • commands that change the connection's state, which outlives the context when the pool lends the connection on, or how its replies are framed: AUTH, HELLO, SELECT, CLIENT, RESET, QUIT, READONLY, READWRITE, ASKING, SCRIPT DEBUG;
      • commands that take the connection out of request and reply: SUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE, SSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PUNSUBSCRIBE, SUNSUBSCRIBE, MONITOR, SYNC, PSYNC, REPLCONF;
      • blocking commands, which hold the connection in a pipeline, so that closing the context waits for them, and don't block inside MULTI: BLPOP, BRPOP, BRPOPLPUSH, BLMOVE, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN, BZPOPMAX, BZMPOP, WAITAOF, DEBUG SLEEP, and XREAD or XREADGROUP with BLOCK.

      Some of these may be allowed in a later release, such as the GRAPH.* commands that don't touch a graph. Other commands are sent as they are: an overwrite of the graph's key, such as a SET of it, or its expiry, still leaves the schema cache as it was, as a change by another client would. In a cluster the context's connection is to the node that serves the graph's key, so a command on a key in another hash slot fails with a MOVED error; put the graph's name in the key as a hash tag to keep it on that node.

      Parameters:
      command - the command's name, such as "SET"
      args - its arguments, as bytes
      Returns:
      the reply
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the command is refused, command is null or empty, or args or one of its elements is null; nothing is queued then

    • sync

      void sync()
      Reads the replies to every command queued so far, without decoding them: each is decoded when its Reply is read. A deleteGraph() that ran clears the schema cache now. The pipeline can be used again afterwards, unless the read failed. Once the context is closed, which read the replies the pipeline awaited, there is nothing to do.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the pipeline is closed or a read of it failed before, if it awaits replies while another pipeline or transaction on the context does too, or if the context was closed before the replies this one awaits were read

    • syncAndReturnAll

      List<@Nullable Object> syncAndReturnAll()
      Reads and decodes the replies to every command queued since the last read, in order. The pipeline can be used again afterwards, unless the read failed.
      Returns:
      the decoded replies, as their Replys return them: an element is null where the reply is nil, and the exception reading the reply throws, a GraphException or the failure of a lookup decoding needed, where the command failed or its reply can't be decoded. Unmodifiable
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the pipeline is closed or a read of it failed before, if it awaits replies while another pipeline or transaction on the context does too, or if the context was closed before the replies this one awaits were read

    • close

      void close()
      Reads the replies the pipeline awaits, as sync() does, and closes the pipeline: it can't be used afterwards, and closing it again does nothing. There is nothing to read once the context is closed, which has read them, and after a read of the pipeline failed the context's connection is closed instead of going back to the pool. The context's connection otherwise stays open.

      Unlike Closeable.close(), this throws no checked exception. It can still throw an unchecked one: an IllegalStateException if another pipeline or transaction on the context awaits replies, or a FalkorDBConnectionException if the connection fails.
